summary: History of phrenology, the skull-reading pseudoscience founded by Franz Joseph Gall around 1800, and how it was used to justify slavery, Native removal and colonialism, fed a trade in Aboriginal bones and shaped Rwanda's ethnic ID cards.

evidence.note: Gall invents cranioscopy in 1800, the start of the story proper
Gall driven out of Austria, moves to France in 1805; Institute of France review 1808
phrenology first succeeds in Britain as justification for empire, especially over the Irish
Kentucky slaveholder Caldwell lectures across the South using phrenology to defend slavery
Morton's 1839 Crania Americana used to justify Indian removal
start of long segment on the Australian trade in Aboriginal skulls and bodies
Ramsay Smith morgue inquiry in Adelaide, 1903; he dies in 1937
Belgian Congo bone collecting and the cannibalism myth
Belgian racial ID cards in Rwanda from 1933, used to target Tutsi in the 1994 genocide
legacy segment on The Bell Curve and scientific racism into the 2010s

notes: Aristotle, Linnaeus, Camper and Blumenbach are pre-story background and not counted in covered_span. Origin AT reflects Gall developing the practice in Vienna (he was born in Baden, DE). main_span runs from cranioscopy to the 1903 Ramsay Smith inquiry, the core 19th-century heyday; the Rwanda legacy extends covered_span to 1994, and the Bell Curve segment sets reaches_present.
